Subject: Defining billable units for Hosted API

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a clear statement we can include in the contract around how usage is metered for the Hosted API. Two specific items:

1) Streaming responses: when our UI subscribes and receives partial tokens via the stream, are those intermediate tokens billed immediately or do you bill only the final completed output? In other words, is there any double-counting for streaming frames vs final message?

2) Rounding/proration: if a response emits fractional timing or partial token units (edge-case with adaptive tokenization), how is rounding applied? Do you round per-response, per-minute, per-request, or use a daily aggregation window?

For context, we plan to run a pilot at ~120M tokens/month and expect to ramp to 1.2B within 6 months if the latency/cost profile holds. Procurement wants to understand the discount ladder and whether any unused commit true-ups apply.

Can you send proposed contract language and a simple pricing grid we can circulate?

Thanks —
Maria Sanchez
Director, AI Products
Atlas Health

Maria —

Appreciate the clear questions. High level answers up front and then attachments with details: see attached proposed-pricing-grid.xlsx and SOW-draft-v2.pdf.

Quick summary:
- Streaming: we bill tokens based on final emitted tokens (input + output). Intermediate stream frames are not billed separately — billing uses the final emitted token count for the request. If a client cancels mid-stream, we bill the tokens emitted up to cancellation.
- Rounding: billing is performed per-request and rounded up to the nearest whole token. For streaming, the fractional emission timing does not create fractional tokens; tokens are integral and we round at the request boundary.
- Commit tiers (proposal):
  * Bronze: 0–500M tokens/month — list price (no commit discount)
  * Silver: 500M–2B tokens/month — 15% off list
  * Gold: 2B+ tokens/month — 28% off list
  * Custom enterprise: committed volumes >5B — negotiated pricing and SLA

We can offer a 6-month ramp credit during the pilot (50% bill-back of overage in months 1–3) as an introductory concession, then standard commit true-up rules apply monthly. True-ups credit unused committed tokens up to a 2-month carry-forward window (this can be tightened in the contract if procurement prefers).

Action items:
1) Aditya — can you confirm the exact per-request rounding clause language we should include (technical billing semantics)?
2) Laura — can you draft a short contract paragraph for "Billable Units & Rounding" that matches the above semantics and the true-up language?
3) Maria — will upload PO if the pricing grid looks ok; we can follow with DocuSign link for SOW.

Thanks,

Hi all —

Thanks for pulling this together, Vanessa. A few technical clarifications from the billing side to ensure contract language is precise:

1) Billable tokens definition: billable_tokens = count(input_tokens) + count(output_tokens) as measured by Redwood's tokenization pipeline at the time the response is completed (or at cancellation). We use a deterministic tokenizer (model-family-aware) and record token counts per request in the billing event.

2) Streaming specifics: streaming frames are transport-level events. We do not create separate billing events for frames. Instead, the billing event for a streaming request is generated when the request completes or is cancelled, using the total emitted output token count. If the customer implements partial reads that result in cancellation, billing is for tokens emitted up to cancel time.

3) Rounding + aggregation: rounding is applied per-request (each request's token count is rounded up to the nearest whole token). Aggregation across requests for tiering is done monthly on billed token totals; there is no per-second rounding.

4) Edge case — retransmits / retries: retries of the same logical user request will be billed as separate requests unless the customer implements idempotency keys and Redwood consumes them to coalesce billing within a short window (30s). If procurement needs to avoid double-charges for client retries, we recommend using idempotency tokens; we can add wording to limit coalescing to retries with identical idempotency keys within 30s.

Suggested short clause for billing appendix (technical):
"Billable Units: Billable units are measured as the sum of input and output tokens produced by Redwood's tokenization pipeline at the time a request is completed or at the time the request is cancelled by the client. Tokens are integral units; each request's token total will be rounded up to the nearest whole token prior to aggregation for billing. Streaming transport frames are not separately billed; only the final emitted output token count for the request is used. Retries will be billed as separate requests unless an idempotency key is provided and honored by Redwood within a 30-second window."

Happy to refine language if legal asks for a different threshold on idempotency window.

—Aditya
Billing/Product
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Defining billable units for Hosted API

Maria / team —

I've taken Aditya's suggested language and put together a contract-ready paragraph and a short definitions table. Main points: be explicit about cancellation billing and the idempotency coalescing window. I attached contract-clause-draft.docx for Procurement's redlines.

Proposed contract paragraph (editable):
"Billable Units and Metering. For purposes of fees under this Agreement, 'Billable Units' shall mean the integral count of tokens produced by Redwood's tokenization pipeline and shall equal the sum of (a) tokens in the request payload and (b) tokens in the final emitted response. Billing events are recorded at the time a request completes or when a request is cancelled by the customer; streaming transport frames are not separately billed. Token counts are rounded up to the nearest whole token on a per-request basis prior to aggregation. Retries will be billed as separate requests unless the customer supplies an idempotency key and Redwood consumes an identical idempotency key within thirty (30) seconds, in which case Redwood will consolidate billing to a single request. Unused committed tokens may be carried forward for up to two (2) subsequent billing cycles as set forth in the pricing schedule."

If Procurement requests a longer carry-forward or different true-up cadence (quarterly vs monthly), mark the redlines and we can discuss commercial trade-offs (e.g., lower tier discounts vs longer carry-forward).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
